item.title: Valencia FC Women’s Team Coach, Three Children Missing in Indonesia Boat Accident
item.description: Jakarta. Fernando Martín, a coach with Spanish football club Valencia FC’s women’s team, and three of his children are missing after their boat sank off Labuan Bajo in East Nusa Tenggara on Friday evening. In a social media post, Valencia FC expressed condolences, saying local authorities had confirmed the deaths. Search efforts for the victims continued on Sunday. item.title: Indonesia’s EV Adoption Surpasses the US for First Time, New Research Finds
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia’s electric vehicle penetration has surpassed that of the United States for the first time, marking a major milestone in the country’s clean-energy transition, according to new research by Ember Energy. Electric vehicles now account for more than 15% of total new car sales in Indonesia this year, the London-based think tank said. item.title: Government Moves 1,882 High-Risk Prisoners to Maximum-Security Facility
item.description: Jakarta. item.title: Family of Missing Spanish Tourists Heads to Indonesia as Search Continues
item.description: Jakarta. Relatives of four Spanish tourists missing off eastern Indonesia are traveling to the country to monitor and support ongoing search efforts, a family spokesperson said on Sunday, as rescue teams continue to battle challenging sea conditions. item.title: Two Helicopters Collide Midair in New Jersey
item.description: Hammonton, New Jersey. One person was killed and another was left critically injured after two helicopters crashed in southern New Jersey on Sunday, officials said. item.title: Post-Christmas, Jakarta Shares Open Higher on Foreign Inflows
item.description: Jakarta. Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) opened modestly higher after the Christmas break on Friday, rising 8 points or 0.09% to 8,545, moving within a range of 8,545–8,573. In the first five minutes of trading, volume reached 2.6 billion shares, with turnover of Rp 1.4 trillion ($83.46 million) and more than 233,000 transactions recorded. item.title: ‘Not Enough Planes’: Bali Govt on Fewer Domestic Tourists
item.description: Jakarta. Bali Governor I Wayan Koster recently attributed the decline in the year-end domestic travelers to a shortage of planes. Koster said that some planes had to undergo their regular maintenance work, thereby prompting Indonesian airlines to operate at a smaller capacity during the year-end holidays. item.title: Indonesian Rescuers Find Body of One Missing Spanish Tourist Off Labuan Bajo
item.description: Labuan Bajo. Indonesian search and rescue teams on Monday recovered the body of a Spanish woman during the fourth day of operations following the sinking of the vessel Putri Sakinah in waters off Labuan Bajo. The body was found at 6:05 a.m. local time near Serai Island, according to authorities. item.title: Fire at Nursing Home in Manado Kills 16 Elderly Residents
item.description: Manado. A fire tore through a nursing home in Manado, North Sulawesi, late Sunday, killing 16 elderly residents, authorities said. The death toll represents half of the facility’s occupants at the time of the incident. The blaze broke out at 8:24 p.m. local time (12:24 p.m. GMT) and spread rapidly through the building, which housed dozens of senior residents. item.title: Gold Prices at Antam Recover, Eyes Year-End Global Upside
item.description: Jakarta. Gold prices at state-owned miner Aneka Tambang, or Antam, rebounded on Monday after a sharp correction over the weekend, tracking volatile global bullion movements toward year-end. Data from Logam Mulia showed Antam’s gold price rose Rp 30,000 to Rp 2,413,000 ($143.86) per gram on Monday, Dec. 29.
